pending_limits: One host and three pairs are a screening experiment, not broad performance generalization.
Ordinary OS/user background activity is uncontrolled; CPU counter storage units do not establish tight accounting precision.
Full process CPU window covers launch through join, while setup/prefill and trace serialization are outside it.
Grant/source-age/wake observations are conservative brackets and supplied-clock checks, not exact linearization or hard deadlines.
ABI object and reserved-capacity accounting excludes opaque OS mutex/CV allocation and does not measure process RSS.
Traces cannot prove instrumentation omitted no work or counter increments; source/binary hashes bind the reviewed implementation.
No radio IQ decoding, RF, Android runtime, decoder accuracy or APK/EXE application-default promotion is tested.
Native notifier timeout/counter-exhaustion and standard-library lock/wait exception injection remain untested; impossibility controls are synthetic.

interpretation_and_next_hypothesis.purpose: Independent read-only interpretation of the completed fixed six-run notification screen; no new performance execution and no application integration.

scope.host: Existing Windows host; GetProcessTimes aggregate process CPU

interpretation: The CPU screen is negative under its original gates. A 5.98% median reduction and one CPU-winning pair do not satisfy the declared 10% and two-of-three requirements. No pair was replaced or rerun in this analysis.

Notification removed 2,374,597 observed normal stage loads and 2,372,797 yields across the three candidate-equivalent workloads. Those counts demonstrate the intended control-flow change, not the CPU cost of each iteration.

All three notification runs reduced complete producer-work p99, while both modes verified 900 of 900 requests and had zero complete producer-work intervals longer than 10 ms. This favorable secondary result does not override the failed primary CPU gates.

Wait p99 stayed between about 16.55 and 17.09 ms for polling and 16.68 to 16.70 ms for notification. Most requests completed the recorded wait in under 2 ms; longer tails occurred under both mechanisms. This is not evidence of faster radio synchronization.

Producer generation median was about 0.641 to 0.643 ms in both modes. Its p99 fell from about 1.454 to 1.468 ms with polling to 1.077 to 1.208 ms with notification. The non-generation owner-work median remained about 0.054 ms, with p99 about 0.130 to 0.139 ms. The coincident tail changes are descriptive; scheduling, power, cache and observer effects were not attributed.

Timed append p99 was about 0.110 to 0.114 ms across these runs. Individual service-call p99 was about 0.0063 to 0.0068 ms; each owner iteration makes at most three. Notification-call p99 was about 0.019 to 0.025 ms. These are wall-clock brackets and neither CPU samples nor additive p99 components.

Exact-byte verification median was about 13.43 to 13.53 ms with polling and 13.90 to 14.06 ms with notification. This synthetic verifier is a large observed consumer interval, but its CPU share and the cause of the difference are unknown.

Owner wake-offset p99 was about 24 to 26 ms even though owner-work p99 stayed below 1.6 ms. A host scheduling gap and measured processing duration are different quantities; these synthetic late starts do not establish dropped hardware IQ or decode failures.

next_single_bounded_experiment.name: Per-thread CPU attribution before further IQ-storage optimization
next_single_bounded_experiment.status: Proposal only; no implementation or execution in this analysis
next_single_bounded_experiment.hypothesis: With source algorithms, payload, verifier and request schedule fixed, notification reduces consumer-thread CPU by at least 10% in median and in at least two of three fixed pairs. Producer/control CPU and sampled stacks can then test whether the aggregate failure reflects offsetting work or a small polling contribution.
next_single_bounded_experiment.reason: The current screen proves that polling disappeared, yet aggregate CPU gains were inconsistent. Existing nested wall-clock intervals cannot resolve which thread or function consumed that CPU.
bounded_plan: Create a separate observer revision that changes only attribution instrumentation. Retain all existing safety, identity, memory, byte-verification and fixed-screen checks; freeze source, executable, compiler, symbols and host recipe before collecting new evidence.

Record raw user and kernel CPU counters for producer and consumer with GetThreadTimes at worker entry and after their final cleanup, plus main/control endpoints nested inside the existing process-CPU window. Keep success/error codes and before/after steady-clock brackets. Do not use std::clock or wall duration as thread CPU.

Keep the aggregate GetProcessTimes window from before launch through join as the existing primary measurement. Declare worker bootstrap/teardown and main measurement-edge exclusions; report any process-versus-thread residual as coverage/accounting information, never force equality or subtract wall-clock intervals from CPU.

After short correctness and failure tests, predeclare exactly three 30-second pairs in the same rotated order. Preserve every result without optional stopping, retries to improve outcomes, altered storage code or parameter tuning.

Collect one additional fixed diagnostic pair with Windows Performance Recorder/Analyzer CPU Sampled and CPU Precise data, stable thread identities and symbol provenance. Keep profiler runs separate from the six counter-only runs. Attribute sampled stacks to generator, verifier, polling/yield and notifier where symbol resolution permits; inspect running, ready and waiting states.

Stop the attribution experiment after the fixed budget. A missing API measurement, invalid counter scope or failed structural check makes that run inconclusive or failed; it does not authorize a favorable replacement.
falsification_and_decision_rules: The consumer-CPU hypothesis fails if its median notification/poll ratio exceeds 0.90 or fewer than two pairs reduce consumer CPU. A reduction confined to wall-clock percentiles is insufficient.

If consumer CPU falls but aggregate CPU does not, inspect measured producer/control counters and separate profiler evidence before proposing a mechanism. Do not infer that the reduction was offset by a particular component without those observations.
Sampled stack attribution is diagnostic, not exact function CPU accounting; absent symbols or sparse samples leave attribution unresolved.
Passing the attribution hypothesis alone does not promote notification into the app, change the original failed screen result, or establish an RF advantage.
limits: GetThreadTimes exposes kernel/user execution amounts in 100 ns storage units, not a documented 100 ns accounting accuracy guarantee.

Counter endpoint intervals differ from the outer process window and include different bootstrap/cleanup edges. CPU totals across separate threads can be compared only with these scope differences explicit.

Profiling changes the workload and periodic sampling can miss short operations. CPU Precise context-switch evidence can help distinguish runnable delay from active execution without making the existing source brackets exact instants.

alternative_priority_if_storage_utility_.recommendation: Redirect effort to actual digital-radio acquisition and recovery benchmarks instead of another storage optimization.
alternative_priority_if_storage_utility_.bounded_test: Use a fixed authorized DMR/NXDN/P25 IQ corpus with known clean frames and controlled SNR, frequency offset, timing error, overlap and sample gaps. Compare the current receiver with one explicit acquisition/recovery change against identical held-out inputs.
primary_outcomes: Time and sample index to first independently valid frame
Correct CRC/FEC-validated frame yield and false-lock rate
Recovery after a declared gap or late acquisition
CPU per active channel and bounded queue/drop counts
alternative_priority_if_storage_utility_.history_utility_gate: Require a controlled delayed-detection/replay case in which bounded history recovers additional correct frames relative to the existing no-history path, within a preregistered latency/memory budget and without false-frame regression. Until that is demonstrated, the synthetic storage path is infrastructure whose receiver benefit remains unmeasured.
alternative_priority_if_storage_utility_.scope_limit: No claim about clearer speech, stronger decryption, GPU benefit or outperforming another SDR follows from the current storage/notification traces.

primary_source_notes.title: Microsoft GetThreadTimes
primary_source_notes.supports: Per-thread user/kernel execution counters, API error handling, and FILETIME 100 ns representation. Storage granularity does not establish empirical accuracy.

primary_source_notes.title: Microsoft CPU Analysis
primary_source_notes.supports: Sampled CPU can group thread/function/stack observations and miss short activity between samples. CPU Precise records context-switch information for running, ready and waiting interpretation.

analysis_limits: Read-only calculations over the completed six-run evidence; no new observer, RF test, timing run or source change.
Per-run p50/p95/p99 use the nearest-rank rule and are not pooled across runs. Component quantiles are not subtracted from or added to one another.
Owner leaf wall-clock intervals and consumer intervals can overlap across threads and contain scheduling delays. No CPU attribution is computed from them.

CSV and sidecar bytes were read once each for this analysis and their hashes matched the report before extraction. The source report hash is retained; this is not a fresh independent build/CI validation.

The profile is one synthetic source workload on one Windows host, three pairs, one sample format and immediate release. It is not a general reliability or speed guarantee for Android, other hosts, real SDR drivers, multiple channels or real decoders.
API memory reservations exclude opaque standard-library synchronization allocations and unrelated process memory; no process RSS or memory-saving claim is made.

Existing eligibility and exact-byte checks support trace correctness within declared instrumentation limits; they do not prove internal state-machine linearization or that no unrecorded source operation exists.

pending: Native forced notifier safety timeout and standard-library synchronization exceptions
Opaque OS/CV allocation and causal per-thread CPU attribution
limits: Deterministic CF32-sized opaque bytes, not RF waveforms or multi-channel decoding.
Three paired rounds are an engineering screen, not a significance estimate.
Normal polling has measured counter instrumentation; no historical CPU comparator used.
Full owner wall intervals include extra notification work; wall time is not CPU time.
Source and observer memory scopes remain separate and exclude opaque runtime allocations; not RSS.
Frozen cores, former studies, application defaults/settings and released artifacts unchanged.
